detail.answer:
1. ROOT CAUSE: The `gitsome` package depends on `feedparser`, whose `setup.py` uses the deprecated `use_2to3` command (removed in modern setuptools/Python 3.12+). The project's metadata only supports up to Python 3.7, but the README does not prevent installation on newer Python versions, causing a build failure on Python 3.14.

detail.answer:
1. ROOT CAUSE: The `gitsome` package depends on `feedparser<6.0.0,>=5.2.1`, and feedparser 5.2.1's `setup.py` uses the deprecated `use_2to3` command which was removed in setuptools ≥58. The verification script ran `pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel`, which upgraded setuptools from 47.1.0 (working) to 68.0.0 (broken), causing the feedparser metadata generation to fail.

2. README PATCH:
```diff
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -420,6 +420,15 @@ If you are not installing in a `virtualenv`, you might need to run with `sudo`:
     $ sudo -H pip3 install gitsome
 
 #### `pip3`
+Depending on your setup, you might also want to run `pip3` with the [`-H flag`](http://stackoverflow.com/a/28619739):
+
+    $ sudo -H pip3 install gitsome
+
+For most linux users, `pip3` can be installed on your system using the `python3-pip` package.
+
+For example, Ubuntu users can run:
+
+    $ sudo apt-get install python3-pip
+
+See this [ticket](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/issues/4) for more details.
+
+### Virtual Environment Installation
+
+You can install Python packages in a [`virtualenv`](http://docs.python-guide.org/en/latest/dev/virtualenvs/) to avoid potential issues with dependencies or permissions.
+
+If you are a Windows user or if you would like more details on `virtualenv`, check out this [guide](http://docs.python-guide.org/en/latest/dev/virtualenvs/).
+
+Install `virtualenv` and `virtualenvwrapper`:
+
+    $ pip3 install virtualenv
+    $ pip3 install virtualenvwrapper
+    $ export WORKON_HOME=~/.virtualenvs
+    $ source /usr/local/bin/virtualenvwrapper.sh
+
+Create a `gitsome` `virtualenv` and install `gitsome`:
+
+    $ mkvirtualenv gitsome
+    $ pip3 install gitsome
+
+If the `pip` install does not work, you might be running Python 2 by default.  Check what version of Python you are running:
+
+    $ python --version
+
+If the call above results in Python 2, find the path for Python 3:
+
+    $ which python3  # Python 3 path for mkvirtualenv's --python option
+
+Install Python 3 if needed.  Set the Python version when calling `mkvirtualenv`:
+
+    $ mkvirtualenv --python [Python 3 path from above] gitsome
+    $ pip3 install gitsome
+
+If you want to activate the `gitsome` `virtualenv` again later, run:
+
+    $ workon gitsome
+
+To deactivate the `gitsome` `virtualenv`, run:
+
+    $ deactivate
+
+### Running as a Docker Container
+
+You can run gitsome in a Docker container to avoid installing Python and `pip3` locally. To install Docker check out the [official Docker documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/getstarted/step_one/#step-1-get-docker).
+
+Once you have docker installed you can run gitsome:
+
+    $ docker run -ti --rm mariolet/gitsome
+
+You can use Docker volumes to let gitsome access your working directory, your local .gitsomeconfig and .gitconfig:
+
+    $ docker run -ti --rm -v $(pwd):/src/              \
+       -v ${HOME}/.gitsomeconfig:/root/.gitsomeconfig  \
+       -v ${HOME}/.gitconfig:/root/.gitconfig          \
+       mariolet/gitsome
+
+If you run this command often you will probably want to define an alias:
+
+    $ alias gitsome="docker run -ti --rm -v $(pwd):/src/              \
+                      -v ${HOME}/.gitsomeconfig:/root/.gitsomeconfig  \
+                      -v ${HOME}/.gitconfig:/root/.gitconfig          \
+                      mariolet/gitsome"
+
+To build the Docker image from sources:
+
+    $ git clone https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome.git
+    $ cd gitsome
+    $ docker build -t gitsome .
+
+### Running the `gh configure` Command
+
+To properly integrate with GitHub, you must first configure `gitsome`:
+
+    $ gh configure
+
+For GitHub Enterprise users, run with the `-e/--enterprise` flag:
+
+    $ gh configure -e
+
+### Enabling Bash Completions
+
+To enable bash completions for `gh` commands outside of `gitsome`, run:
+
+    $ gh configure --bash-completion
+
+This will output the completion script. Add it to your `.bashrc`:
+
+    $ gh configure --bash-completion >> ~/.bashrc
+    $ source ~/.bashrc
+
+### Enabling `gh` Tab Completions Outside of `gitsome`
+
+The `gh` command supports tab completions in bash and zsh. To enable them:
+
+#### For Bash Users
+
+    $ gh configure --bash-completion >> ~/.bashrc
+    $ source ~/.bashrc
+
+#### For Zsh Users
+
+    $ gh configure --zsh-completion >> ~/.zshrc
+    $ source ~/.zshrc
+
+### Optional: Installing `PIL` or `Pillow`
+
+Displaying the avatar for the `gh me` and `gh user` commands will require installing the optional `PIL` or `Pillow` dependency.
+
+Windows* and Mac:
+
+    $ pip3 install Pillow
+
+*See the [Windows Support](#windows-support) section for limitations on the avatar.
+
+Ubuntu users can run:
+
+    $ sudo apt-get install python3-pil
+
+### Supported Python Versions
+
+`gitsome` supports Python 3.4 through 3.7. Python 3.8+ is not supported due to a dependency (`feedparser`) that uses deprecated setuptools APIs.
+
+### Supported Platforms
+
+`gitsome` is available for Mac, Linux, Unix, [Windows](#windows-support), and [Docker](#running-as-docker-container).
+
+### Windows Support
+
+`gitsome` works on Windows via the `gitsome.bat` script. The `gh` commands work in cmd.exe and PowerShell.
+
+## Developer Installation
+
+### Continuous Integration
+
+`gitsome` uses Travis CI for continuous integration. See [.travis.yml](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/blob/master/.travis.yml) for details.
+
+### Unit Tests and Code Coverage
+
+Run unit tests with:
+
+    $ python tests/run_tests.py
+
+Code coverage is tracked via Codecov. See [codecov.yml](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/blob/master/codecov.yml).
+
+### Documentation
+
+Documentation is generated from docstrings. See [scripts/update_docs.sh](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/blob/master/scripts/update_docs.sh).
+
+## Contributing
+
+Contributions are welcome! Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines.
+
+## Credits
+
+* [xonsh](https://github.com/scopatz/xonsh) - The Python-powered shell that powers `gitsome`
+* [prompt_toolkit](https://github.com/prompt-toolkit/python-prompt-toolkit) - For the autocompletion and interactive help
+* [click](https://github.com/pallets/click) - For the `gh` command CLI
+* [requests](https://github.com/psf/requests) - For GitHub API communication
+* [feedparser](https://github.com/kurtmckee/feedparser) - For parsing GitHub feeds
+* [pygments](https://github.com/pygments/pygments) - For syntax highlighting
+* [ply](https://github.com/dabeaz/ply) - For the Python lexer/parser
+
+## Contact Info
+
+* Donne Martin - [@donnemartin](https://github.com/donnemartin)
+
+## License
+
+Apache 2.0 - See [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/blob/master/LICENSE.txt) for details.
```
